title: What's Up With Monday's Weakness?
summary:
What's Up With Monday's Weakness? 

             
             
            Bonds were moderately weaker on Monday and not in a way that was obviously connected to any of the potential scapegoats. We know that there was selling in the EU bond market overnight and while U.S. yields correlated with much of that move, that correlation broke down precisely when an EU-driven move would have been most relevant. It's easier to blame an ongoing recovery in the tech space even though there's a similar lack of elegant correlation between tech stocks and bond yields. Bottom line: Treasuries benefited from last week's moments of highest concern surrounding the tech sector. Since then, when those concerns have been anything less than dire, bond yields have cautiously drifted higher.

title: Mortgage Rates Start Week Higher
summary: Mortgage rates were moderately higher to start the new week, adding to the modest losses seen on Friday. The silver lining is that any of the past 3 business days saw the lowest rates since September 23rd.  There were no clear reasons for today's rate movement in terms of economic reports or news headlines. The same was true for last week's biggest swings which were driven by broad bond market sentiment as traders sought safer havens due to concerns about a pull-back in the tech sector.  On that note, tech stocks had their best day in several weeks today with much of the improvement already intact by the time the domestic trading session began. As the week progresses, that same "broad market sentiment" could continue to be a driving force because there aren't any big ticket events on the economic calendar.  In nuts and bolts terms, the average top tier 30yr fixed rate is back up to 7.43%, 0.06% higher than Friday's latest levels and  0.10% higher than Thursday's low of 7.33.  [thirtyyearmortgagerates]

title: Light Calendar Leaves Tech Concerns in Focus
summary: Last week's most notable development was a flight to safety in the bond market precipitated by concerns about a shift in tech sector sentiment. The shift in question was mainly driven by Coreweave which saw shares plummet and corporate debt spreads explode. That cause some concern about spillover to the rest of the tech sector. Treasuries benefited not only only from general safe haven demand, but also because the tech jitters implied a slower pace of AI capex and corporate debt issuance (both of which had previously created upward pressure on bond yields). The NASDAQ is starting the new week well off Friday afternoon's lows and 10yr yields have retreated accordingly. That said, Treasuries remain ready to benefit from any resurgence in AI sector jitters. In the absence of any high-impact economic data, assessing that risk will be this week's main theme.

summary: For many loan officers, building their own brokerage is the right path. title: Title Resources Group Names Robert Greenbaum EVP To Lead Customer Experience
summary: Title Resources Group (TRG) has appointed Robert Greenbaum, executive vice president, to lead its customer experience efforts, adding a veteran of mortgage marketing, sales, and customer acquisition to its leadership team.The title insurance underwriter announced the appointment Oct. 19. Greenbaum most recently served as chief marketing officer for AAFMAA Mortgage Services, where he led marketing and sales strategies.

title: First Horizon Restructures Origination, Stands By Warehouse Lending
summary: First Horizon, a Memphis-based regional bank operating across 12 Southern states, has agreed to sell approximately $4.5 billion of lower-yielding residential mortgages while restructuring its mortgage operation to focus production more closely on core banking clients.Management separately reaffirmed its commitment to warehouse lending, giving independent mortgage bankers an important distinction: the bank is repositioning its residential portfolio while continuing to finance other lenders.

title: Rates Above 7% Shrink Buyer Budgets In Loosening Housing Market
summary: Buyers have more room to negotiate a home purchase, but less borrowing power to bring to the table.The average 30-year fixed rate rose from 6.66% in late August to 7.40% in early October, reducing the loan amount supported by a fixed monthly principal-and-interest budget by about 7.2%. That financing squeeze accompanies a housing market increasingly tilted toward buyers, according to Realtor.com’s latest Market Clock report, released Oct. 19.

title: VantageScore Expands Credit Planning Push With New Simulator
summary: VantageScore has introduced a mortgage credit score simulator designed to help lenders and loan originators evaluate how changes to a borrower’s credit profile could affect their VantageScore 4.0 scores.Announced Oct. 16, the tool generates projected scores using the actual VantageScore 4.0 algorithm and credit files from Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion, according to the company.

title: Bay Capital Adds LiteSpeed To Its Pitch For Producing LOs
summary: Bay Capital Mortgage Corporation has deployed LenderLogix’s LiteSpeed point-of-sale platform, adding borrower applications, document management, electronic signatures, and other origination tools to a technology offering it markets to prospective loan officers.The Annapolis, Maryland-based mortgage banker announced the deployment Oct. 19. LiteSpeed integrates with Encompass and allows borrowers to apply, upload documents, and complete tasks through a mobile-friendly interface.
